newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end lower, below 20,000 on strong yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end lower, below 20,000 on strong yen.

text.p: Tokyo stocks ended lower in the Friday session, closing below the 20,000 threshold for the first time this week. Brokers said profit-taking by both foreign and domestic institutional investors hit the major indices as the yen strengthened against the dollar.
The 225-share Nikkei average fell 259.03 points or 1.29 percent to 19,802.78. June Nikkei futures slid 230 to 19,830.

"Currencies provided a cue for investors who had been buying blue chips lately to start correcting," said Noboru Yorita, general manager at Tachibana Securities. "How fast the buying resumes, or when it does, will depend on the yen."

The yen's climb past 123 yen to the dollar for the first time in about a month prompted investors to sell export-strong issues which had played a major part in boosting the Nikkei average by about 10 percent since the new business year started on April 1.
"Buying interest shifted to import-reliant shares which benefit from a stronger yen today due to currencies," said Yasuo Ueki, general manager at Nikko Securities.
Electrical issues declined, with TDK Corp shedding 180 yen to 9,090. Advantest Corp slumped 160 yen to 7,010. Sony Corp fell 200 yen to 9,520.
"Sony was hit, but not as much as some of the others as it was supported by solid earnings announced on Thursday," one broker said. "Investors are waiting for bargain hunting opportunities."
On the other hand, shares in sectors such as oil 0#OIL.T, which are dependent on imports, rose on speculation by dealers that raw material costs would fall because of the strong yen.
Nippon Oil Co Ltd added five yen to 630, the second most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse with 7.64 million shares. Showa Shell Sekiyu KK rose 10 yen to 961.

The oil sector was at the top of the list of gaining sectors, followed by pulp/paper, real estate, fisheries and credit/lease. The retreaters were led by precision instruments, rubber, automobiles, electrical equipment and gas.
First section turnover totalled 463 million shares, up slightly from 417 million shares on the previous day.

Brokers said that actual trade was subdued ahead of the weekend and amid uncertainty over yen/dollar rates. The volume figure was inflated by activity related to the May options settlement, they added. After the market closed the Osaka Securities Exchange said the settlement was at 20,276.83.
Losers outnumbered winners 728 issues to 369, while 160 issues were unchanged.
In other indices, the TOPIX index fell 16.87 points or 1.13 percent to 1,478.04. The Nikkei 300 shed 3.61 points or 1.24 percent to end at 287.22.
The second section index added 1.61 points or 0.09 percent to 1,715.43. Turnover was 9.92 million shares, against 10.02 million on Thursday.
The over-the-counter index had weakened 2.98 points or 0.25 percent to 1,173.99 by late Tokyo trade.
But despite the weakening OTC index, drugstore giant Matsumotokiyoshi Co Ltd was at a new high for the calendar year at 4,140, up from 3,820 at Thursday's close.

"The earnings revision announced on Thursday helped the share price," said a trader at a foreign securities house. "Buying was also prompted by the fact that the firm felt little impact from the rise in the national sales tax."
The drugstore forecast a parent current profit of 6.68 billion yen in the 1996/97 fiscal year, up from the previous forecast of 5.30 billion yen.
--Masako Iijima, Tokyo Equities Desk (+81-3-3432-9052)
